build_target: Harden the existing enzyme patent screening harness so it reflects the v3 three-layer specification and the build-time Triad patch. The task is to turn the current prototype into a safer Phase 1/Phase 2-ready harness foundation with explicit access control, sanitizer enforcement, recall-first evaluation metrics, raw trace persistence, immutable-area guardrails, a proposal-only Meta-Harness layer, and auditable build artifacts.
requirements_unpacked: Keep Layer 1 production code, Layer 2 harness code, and Layer 3 meta-harness code separated by directory and responsibility.
Enforce Rule 0 data protection before any LLM-facing or filesystem-persisted payload, including recursive structured payloads.
Define a data access control matrix covering patent data, golden set labels, human labels, model outputs, raw traces, protected metrics, build logs, and PII/financial data.
Replace accuracy-first evaluation with recall-first metrics, critical miss tracking, per-category recall, ECE, and data protection violation accounting.
Persist Layer 1 and Layer 2 execution traces in a machine-readable raw filesystem layout for later Layer 3 inspection.
Keep metric definitions, golden set records, sanitizer code, and deployment gate logic outside Layer 3 mutable scope.
Make Layer 3 proposal-only: it may inspect allowed artifacts and produce candidate proposals, but must not overwrite production or harness code directly.
Add deployment gate logic that rejects recall regressions, critical miss increases, category regressions, ECE regressions, data protection violations, and non-Pareto candidates.
Update the Meta-Harness skill file so the Triad rule, mutable/immutable boundaries, and domain constraints are readable and not mojibake.
Strengthen Triad CI verification with explicit exemptions, fake-diversity checks, and atomic-plan checks.
Add focused tests that run without external LLM credentials by using deterministic fallback behavior.

design_approaches.name: Policy-first hardening inside the current Python harness
design_approaches.idea: Add small reusable policy, sanitizer, trace, metric, and gate primitives around the current modules while preserving the existing directory layout and smoke-test style. The prototype remains easy to inspect and can graduate to stricter filesystem permissions later.
design_approaches.libraries_patterns: Python standard library, Pydantic models already present, explicit enum-based policy matrix, JSONL audit and trace files.
design_approaches.pros: Low migration risk, fits the existing codebase, allows offline tests, and makes each v3 control visible in code.
design_approaches.cons: Filesystem permissions are represented as code-level guardrails rather than OS-level mounts in local development.
design_approaches.trade_off: Best for Phase 1 because it builds the control plane without introducing infrastructure complexity prematurely.
design_approaches.coupling_confounds: Touches several modules, so tests must verify that production, harness, and meta-harness responsibilities remain distinct.

design_approaches.name: External orchestration service with strict sandbox mounts
design_approaches.idea: Move evaluation, deployment gate, audit logging, and Layer 3 proposal execution into a separate service that mounts production and harness areas with explicit OS-level permissions.
design_approaches.libraries_patterns: Container profiles, read-only mounts, service-to-service APIs, policy-as-code.
design_approaches.pros: Closest to the eventual production security posture and strongest immutable enforcement.
design_approaches.cons: Too heavy for the current local prototype and would require CI/container work before basic harness behavior is complete.
design_approaches.trade_off: More secure long-term, but slower and harder to validate in this repository right now.
design_approaches.coupling_confounds: Infrastructure changes could obscure whether metric and workflow semantics are correct.

design_approaches.name: Documentation-only architecture pass
design_approaches.idea: Leave the code mostly intact and add the requested matrices, phase checklists, reward-hacking scenarios, and operating rules as architecture documents.
design_approaches.libraries_patterns: Markdown specification and manual review checklist.
design_approaches.pros: Fastest path and useful for stakeholder alignment.
design_approaches.cons: Does not stop unsafe behaviors already present, such as direct Layer 3 overwrites or unsanitized prompt construction.
design_approaches.trade_off: Useful as a supplement, not enough for a harness that should actually enforce the v3 constraints.
design_approaches.coupling_confounds: Creates a gap between written policy and executable behavior.

non_obvious_option.name: Defer Layer 3 entirely and only ship Layer 1 plus Layer 2 MVP
non_obvious_option.idea: Remove or disable the existing Meta-Harness agent and focus only on Dataset Curator, Eval Runner, and Reviewer UI style artifacts until the golden set and human trust criteria are mature.
non_obvious_option.why_considered: The v3 roadmap says Phase 1 keeps Layer 3 inactive, and direct self-editing is a significant reward-hacking risk.
non_obvious_option.why_not_selected_as_only_path: The repository already contains a Layer 3 prototype, so replacing it with a safe proposal-only skeleton is better than leaving unsafe code in place.

recommended_for_planning.name: Policy-first hardening inside the current Python harness
recommended_for_planning.reason: It gives the user a working harness structure now, keeps the current code recognizable, and converts the unsafe Layer 3 prototype into a controlled proposal workflow.

recommended_for_planning.name: Documentation-only architecture pass as a companion artifact
recommended_for_planning.reason: The TXT explicitly asks for matrices, reward-hacking scenarios, phase checklists, Triad exemptions, and CI mechanisms; these belong in a concise architecture document alongside executable checks.

explicitly_rejected.name: External orchestration service with strict sandbox mounts
explicitly_rejected.reason: Correct direction for Phase 3 infrastructure, but too large for this local harness construction pass and likely to hide core metric and policy logic behind deployment setup.

explicitly_rejected.name: Keep the direct self-healing code writer
explicitly_rejected.reason: It violates the v3 build-time Triad patch, lets Layer 3 overwrite production code directly, and gives the proposer too much opportunity to game evaluation.

open_questions_for_human: Which exact patent claim categories should be mandatory in the first real golden set beyond percent_identity, Markush, functional_claim, variant_claim, motif_claim, and non_english?
What human approval threshold should trigger mandatory review: changed LOC, touched modules, semantic risk class, or all Layer 3 proposals during Phase 3?
Which enterprise CI system will enforce the Triad gate: GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Azure DevOps, or an internal merge queue?
